title: Quant SLOs: probechain latency-quality matrix and kernel switch behavior
content:
Summary and purpose:

This note captures an ad-hoc investigation into how different quantization strategies (INT8 via AWQ, GPTQ variants, and FP8 profiles) interact with kernel selection and runtime routing under realistic SLO-driven traffic patterns. Goal is to produce actionable guardrails for model routing and kernel warmup so we avoid large p99 regressions during kernel switchover or microburst traffic.

High-level finding (TL;DR):
- AWQ-int8 provides best steady-state tokens/sec for short interactive requests (<=128 tokens) but is most sensitive to kernel mismatch during sudden context length increases (p99 spikes up to 4x baseline).
- GPTQ variants are more quality-stable across long contexts (>=2k) but show 10-25% lower throughput on the lane-optimized kernel family; their p50/p95 remain tight.
- FP8 (mixed) gives the best memory compression for 13B+ models and acceptable quality, but introduces sporadic tail latency when the runtime falls back to a slower GEMM kernel under fragmentation.
- Kernel switchover without coalescing requests or pre-heating KV cache is the single largest contributor to >500ms tail spikes in our probes.

Context and motivation:
Teams keep asking if we can safely use AWQ/INT8 as the default for hosted interactive tiers given its cost benefits. Operations has observed repeated incidents where a long request (or retry) triggers the runtime to pick a different kernel and p99 jumps, causing SLO alerts. We built a small probe harness to reproduce and characterize the problem.

Experiment design (probechain harness):
- Models: 7B open-arch (baseline FP16), 13B transformer (production candidate), 34B test slice (memory-limited scenario).
- Quant variants: AWQ-int8 (pack=4 tiled kernel), GPTQ (layerwise, 8-bit residuals where applicable), FP8 mixed-e4m3 profiles.
- Kernels: lane-optimized (fast short-context), fused-gemm-attn (balanced), scalar-fallback (safe but slow).
- Hardware: A100-80GB (primary), H100-80GB (spot for gradients), and an AMD MI250 node for throughput cross-checks.
- Workloads: interactive-short (mean len=64, p95=128), background-batch (mean len=2048, p95=8192), mixed-burst (90% short, 10% long, bursts simulated every 60s).
- Client harness: 100 simulated clients with poisson arrivals, periodic bursts of 300 concurrent short requests, occasional long tail requests injected to force kernel decision changes.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, GPU memory (MB), delta-LL (log-prob delta relative to FP16 baseline), BERTScore (generation quality proxy), kernel-switch count, KV-cache-miss ratio.

Representative numeric results (abridged):
- 13B model, A100, mixed-burst workload, batchsize=1 scheduling:
  - FP16 baseline (fused-gemm-attn): p50=72ms, p95=160ms, p99=420ms, tokens/sec=920, GPU mem=28GB, BERTScore=0.88
  - AWQ-int8 (lane-optimized): p50=58ms, p95=130ms, p99=1800ms (spiky), tokens/sec=1280, GPU mem=20GB, BERTScore=0.84, kernel-switch_count=avg 0.12/s during bursts, KV-cache-miss=0.37
  - GPTQ (fused-gemm-attn): p50=85ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, tokens/sec=740, GPU mem=22GB, BERTScore=0.872, kernel-switch_count=0.03/s, KV-cache-miss=0.12
  - FP8 mixed (fused-gemm-attn -> scalar-fallback edge): p50=70ms, p95=180ms, p99=950ms, tokens/sec=980, GPU mem=16GB, BERTScore=0.865, kernel-switch_count=0.08/s, KV-cache-miss=0.21

Interpretation of numbers:
- AWQ wins on throughput and memory but its high p99 in mixed traffic came from rapid kernel selection oscillation: short requests prefer lane-optimized kernels; whenever a long request appeared the runtime switched to fused-gemm-attn and then back. During the switch, KV cache entries for the lane-optimized layout were invalidated (format/packing mismatch) causing cache misses and full recompute for subsequent short requests.
- GPTQ preserves quality (lower delta-LL) and keeps kernel selection more consistent (fewer switch events) because its layout matches the fused kernel execution path. The throughput penalty is the tradeoff.
- FP8's sporadic tails were correlated with memory fragmentation and falling back to scalar-fallback kernels on certain batch shapes; this was reproducible under background-batch heavy loads.

Micro-diagnosis: kernel switchover mechanics and KV cache alignment:
- Kernel selection is currently decided per-request at the dispatch layer based on model metadata + request shape. There is no coalescing window, so if two concurrent requests arrive with different preferred kernels the scheduler will assign different worker partitions and may cause warmup thrash.
- KV cache is keyed by model-id + quant-layout-hash. When kernel changes, layout-hash differs, making cached entries inaccessible even if the underlying key sequences overlap. That magnifies the apparent latency when mixed workloads come through.

Quality tradeoff analysis:
- BERTScore deltas vs FP16: AWQ -0.04 (visible but often acceptable for short-chat features); GPTQ -0.008 (near-transparent); FP8 -0.015 (acceptable for embeddings and many generation tasks).
- Delta-LL (bits/token) correlates with human-rated coherence: AWQ shows 0.12 bits/token degradation for a small subset of instruction-following prompts, GPTQ shows 0.03 bits/token.

Operational guidance (recommended immediate guardrails):
1) Short-interactive tier (SLO p99 <=500ms):
   - Default: AWQ-int8 on lane-optimized kernel only if request length <= 256 and client history is warm (KV-cache hit rate > 0.5).
   - If mixed-burst > 15% long requests in a 1m window, fall back to GPTQ fused-gemm-attn for the whole model instance to avoid oscillation.
2) Long-context/Batch tier (throughput-first):
   - Default: GPTQ on fused-gemm-attn. AWQ not recommended for sustained long contexts due to decreasing BERTScore and cache thrash.
3) FP8 usage:
   - Allowed for memory-constrained dedicated nodes; add runtime flag to disable scalar-fallback kernel on critical SLO routes until fragmentation heuristics are in place.
4) Kernel switching behavior:
   - Add a 200ms coalescing window at dispatch for kernel selection to reduce oscillation under concurrent mixed arrivals.
   - Implement a soft migration: do not immediately evict KV-cache entries when layout-hash changes; provide a compatibility shim that can interpret both layouts for a short grace period (configurable, default 30s).

Telemetry and alerting additions (short term):
- Add a kernel_switch_count metric per model-worker and surface this in Console with a p99 alarm if switch_count > 0.2/s per worker over 5m.
- KV-cache-miss ratio spikes should be correlated with p99 latency; add correlated dashboards.

Planned follow-ups and open questions:
- Run a longer A/B (2 week) test on production-like traffic with the 200ms coalescing window to quantify SLO impact. Ticket: ENG-8742.
- Investigate a compact cross-layout cache encoding to avoid full invalidation on kernel switchover. Rough idea: store canonical KV sequence plus layout-conversion metadata. Risk: CPU overhead for conversion; needs microbench.
- Evaluate hybrid routing: run AWQ-int8 for the first N tokens and switch to GPTQ for the remainder of long responses (to amortize startup gains). This requires streaming-aware model slicing.

Draft action items (owners and rough ETA):
- runtime: implement dispatch coalescing window + feature flag (Arjun P) — ETA 2 weeks (PR linked).
- runtime: add kernel_switch_count and kv_cache_miss telemetry (Liam O) — ETA 1 week.
- research: microbench conversion overhead for cross-layout cache shim (Sofia R) — ETA 3 weeks.
- infra: schedule 2-week canary with mixed-burst traffic on a dedicated cluster (Maya C) — ETA 1 month.

Notes to self / open fragments:
- Need to validate whether certain attention kernel implementations (vendor-supplied) expose a layout that is trivially convertible; reach out to HW partners for kernel layout docs.
- Human eval for AWQ failures: set up small rater pool to confirm whether -0.04 BERTScore maps to visible UX regressions.

References and quick links:
- Linear: ENG-8742 kernel switch coalesce (see linked_artifacts).
- PR: runtime dispatch coalesce WIP (see linked_artifacts).

If this looks sensible I will schedule a short sync with runtime infra and research to align on the coalescing window design and telemetry.
